body.statement: There is a universal \(C>0\) such that \(\mathsf A(G,T,e,\delta)\) first determines whether \(d_e(G)<\infty\). On the finite branch it returns exactly \((d_e(G),p_e,\mathcal Q_{G,e},h_{G,e})\), where \(p_e\in K_G[t]\) is monic with rational-circuit coefficients. On the transcendental branch it returns exactly \((\infty,\mathcal N_{G,e})\), where \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\) certifies that the queried-coordinate projection of a positive-dimensional irreducible generic-fiber component is dominant onto \(\mathbb A^1_{K_G}\), and it returns no \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\). In \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\), construction time and certificate length are at most \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\), and total symbolic error probability is at most \(\delta\). On the tree-plus-\(k\) class, the finite branch strictly strengthens the general polynomial-space yes-or-no procedure by returning the coordinate degree and eliminant.
body.justification: A sharp degree frontier becomes operational only with a complete graph-input certificate of the queried minimal polynomial.
body.gap: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma search bounded-degree rational formulas, and Dörfler et al. decide general identification in polynomial space; neither returns algebraic coordinate minimal polynomials with fixed-parameter certificates.
body.consumer: fasttreeid can replace its \(0/1/2\) status by exact higher finite degree and a verifiable branch polynomial for added-parent graphs.

obligation.what_is_open: A complete fixed-parameter implementation proof for both algorithm tags, including the covariance-only circuit descent, every divisor stratum, and the dominance certificate.
obligation.obstruction: Generic rational-univariate theory covers a zero-dimensional sliced system, but it does not by itself prove that the source-prime component and every pole or zero-over-zero stratum can be selected and certified within the claimed \(n^{C(k+1)}\) circuit bound.
obligation.attempted: I reduced the task to at most \(2k\) quadratic variables, bounded the zero-dimensional degree, and derived the multiplication-matrix route to the coordinate minimal polynomial. The missing component-selection and certificate-size analysis is the remaining crux.
obligation.partial_result: The quadratic core has at most \(2k\) variables, polynomially many quadratic equations, and polynomially many recorded divisors. Enumerating independence candidates and divisor strata costs \(n^{O(k+1)}\) identity tests, while every zero-dimensional stratum has degree at most \(2^{2k}\). Over \(K_G(U)\), multiplication by \(\lambda_e\) therefore has size at most \(2^{2k}\); its first matrix linear dependence gives the coordinate minimal polynomial. Pure transcendence shows that polynomial is \(p_e\in K_G[t]\), and a denominator-avoiding evaluation of \(U\) removes directed coordinates from its circuits. What remains unproved is one explicit prime-component algorithm that simultaneously handles all divisors, proves covariance-only descent and slice coverage, emits a checkable transcendence certificate, and bounds every intermediate circuit and PIT degree by \(n^{C(k+1)}\).
